reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes StrongBlock nodes as a way to earn daily passive income and instructs viewers to acquire 10 STRONG tokens before opening a node and collecting rewards. It connects that promotion to wallet funding, transaction approvals, gas charges, a recurring maintenance fee, and projected earnings from multiple nodes, although rewards are described as not guaranteed and the speaker advises due diligence.

if you had five strong nodes it would take you twenty one days to accumulate ten strong

opening.argument: The presentation includes meaningful caution rather than an unconditional promise. The speaker tells viewers to be patient and conduct their own research, while the node-creation screen qualifies the rewards as not guaranteed. The financial discussion is also framed as a calculation exercise: it includes taxes, maintenance, claim fees, and changing assumptions rather than presenting a fixed outcome. That combination supports treating the content as risk-disclosing guidance about a volatile crypto activity, not deceptive certification that viewers will profit.

this is also a pretty good calculator

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title's promotional wording does not establish that the video concealed risk. The narration openly discusses gas charges and a recurring maintenance fee, and the node interface qualifies rewards. Those disclosures undercut the claim that viewers were given an unconditional earnings promise.

citations.quote: Make MONEY DAILY With STRONG NODES! (PASSIVE INCOME)
node is gonna have a 1495 monthly fee

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings and a qualification do not change the central financial pitch. The title expressly pairs Strong nodes with daily passive income, while the tutorial tells viewers how to acquire the required tokens, open a node, and collect rewards. Disclosing fees describes the cost of participation; it does not show that the promoted returns are real or that the opportunity is safe.

opening.argument: The video's dominant form is operational instruction. It walks through adding a token in MetaMask, swapping assets, using the StrongBlock application, creating and editing a node, paying fees, and converting tokens. The speaker repeatedly describes the material as training and explains the mechanics through a personal account, including how to inspect transactions and use a calculator. That is consistent with an educational technology demonstration: showing how an interface and workflow operate is not, by itself, proof that the creator is certifying the service or guaranteeing a viewer-specific result.

so I'm going to show you how to quickly edit your note information
we can show you how to actually convert your strong tokens

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it training is not merely a label: the narration supplies step-by-step interface instructions and explains transaction handling. The title may be promotional, but a promotional title attached to a practical demonstration does not establish that the demonstration itself made a guaranteed claim about viewer outcomes.

citations.quote: one of our cryptonaires training videos

you're gonna click on the application

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format is precisely how the participation pathway is promoted. This is not a detached software lesson: viewers are told they need 10 Strong tokens, shown how to open a node, and instructed how to collect rewards and pay its recurring fee. Demonstrating the steps does not establish that the underlying earnings proposition is legitimate.

citations.quote: you're going to need 10 strong tokens to open a node
how to pay fees, collect rewards
you'll have to pay a 14.95 fee every month to maintain your nodes

opening.argument: The evidence is also compatible with an ordinary paid digital service or product demonstration. The video identifies an application, explains token purchases and swaps, itemizes gas and maintenance charges, and shows the user managing nodes. It does not show a request for passwords or credentials, a downline, or a guaranteed return. The speaker even notes that fees vary and that available funds may be insufficient, which is ordinary transaction disclosure rather than concealment. Presenting a paid service and explaining its costs does not alone establish a scam.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a purchase path and fees, but those features are also consistent with paid software or a token-based service. The narration discloses the monthly fee and explains that gas fees vary widely; nothing in those facts alone establishes a hidden deposit mechanism, credential theft, or a guaranteed return.

When it comes to Gas fees, they range wildly

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is not whether fees are disclosed or whether credentials are requested. The video links payment of tokens and recurring fees to node rewards, calls the result passive income, and offers calculations for recovering an investment. The absence of a password request or downline does not resolve whether this paid node-return mechanism is deceptive.
